- **A) Change the wire**: SIZE_THAT_FITS transmits ALL candidates as children (each child = a candidate). The renderer picks the visible one via container query. FIT_CHANGED still flows for app-side selection state? Actually if all candidates are on the wire, the app no longer strictly needs to swap children on FIT_CHANGED — the renderer already has all candidates. But the FIT_CHANGED is still useful for the app to know the current selection (the app owns retained state). Hmm, actually the spec's whole design is "the app transmits only the selected child; candidates live app-side" — the point being bandwidth: don't transmit unselected subtrees. Transmitting all candidates changes that contract.

- **B) Keep wire as-is (one child), SSR renders all candidates by having access to all of them somehow**. But the Rust HTML renderer is a pure function of the opcode stream — it can only render what's transmitted. The candidates live app-side in the Java/Rust DSL, not on the wire. For SSR, the server builds the HTML from the opcode stream. So SSR cannot know about un-transmitted candidates unless:
  - the emitter emits them all (wire change), or
  - there's a separate SSR-only side channel.

The user explicitly said: "So render all branches of the SizeThatFits and then use css to only render the matching one." and "The container queries should match the Fit's specified." and "And then after first render it should hydrate and work with delta changes afterwards."

So they're proposing to render all branches. This implies a wire change: SizeThatFits children = all candidates. Then the renderer maps each candidate to a container-query-gated wrapper. First paint correct.

But wait — there's tension with the "delta changes afterwards" step. If we simply send all candidates always, then FIT_CHANGED no longer needs to trigger a child swap (all children are always there). The renderer shows the matching one via CSS. FIT_CHANGED becomes purely informational to the app (which may matter for app logic), or possibly still needed to keep the app's `fitIndex` signal in sync so other derived UI reflects it. Actually the app-side retained `fitIndex` still drives app logic (e.g. a computed that depends on which variant is shown), so FIT_CHANGED is still useful. But no TREE swap is needed over the wire after hydration — the candidates are all present from the start.

Hmm, but that contradicts the architecture principle "only changes travel" (an unchanged fit emits zero opcodes). With all-candidates-always model: an unchanged fit → zero opcodes (candidates unchanged). A candidate's content changed → emits that candidate's deltas even if it's not the visible one. That's a real tradeoff: transmitting all candidates means a background candidate's changes ride the wire even while invisible. For the music demo that's fine (small). But it changes the protocol contract.

Alternative middle ground: 
- **A1) Always transmit all candidates.** Cleanest conceptual model; SSR renders all; container queries gate visibility; FIT_CHANGED still flows for app state; no child swap ever. But bandwidth: always all subtrees. Browsers handle display:none fine. Protocol change: children: N (all candidates), plus the renderer uses container queries to show one.
- **A2) Transmit all candidates ONLY in the initial/SSR snapshot, then collapse to one-child + swaps on FIT_CHANGED.** More complex: after first render + connect, the server sends a full snapshot (or the client requests resync) that has only the selected child, and the client replaces the container-query presentation with the single-child delta model. This is messy and would cause a visible flicker/jump when the SSR's all-candidates present becomes one child. Not great.

Actually, let me reconsider what "container queries" buys for the LIVE client vs SSR. Container queries are a CSS feature: `@container (min-width: 640px)` applied to a wrapper gated by the slot. This works for BOTH SSR first paint AND live resize — the browser re-evaluates container queries on resize automatically. So the DOM client could ALSO use container queries instead of ResizeObserver+measure. Then FIT_CHANGED reporting still needs the derived index to send to the app: but actually, if the visible candidate is chosen purely by CSS, the DOM doesn't need to pick anything — the app's `fitIndex` signal... hmm, the app wants to know which one is shown (for its own logic), and to be honest the renderer is supposed to be stateless (must not retain app state). Displaying via container query is fine (it's output selection, arguably layout). But the app still needs FIT_CHANGED to update its retained selection (which other logic may read). And the renderer still needs SOME notion of "which is currently active" to report transitions.

But container queries + ResizeObserver: ResizeObserver on the slot still gives width → fit index → FIT_CHANGED. Or, we could drop the measure and just report the fit when the visible candidate changes (via mutation observer on container query application? awkward). Simplest: keep the existing ResizeObserver + fitIndexFor to report FIT_CHANGED transitions, but let CSS container queries handle VISIBILITY. The reports keep the app's fitIndex in sync (no swap needed if all candidates, or swap is a no-op / never happens).

Wait — if all candidates ride the wire and the DOM shows via container query, do we even need FIT_CHANGED? The app-side retained `fitIndex` drives... in the current Java DSL FitSlot, fitIndex is a WritableSignal class-saved as `node.fitSelection`. Its structuralContent only renders the selected. If we move to "all candidates always present", FitSlot just always renders all candidates and fitIndex is only informational. The emitter's reconcileSlot/restoreFitSelection logic would change to not swap. But keeping FIT_CHANGED is still valuable: the app can bind to the current fit (e.g. a computed signal) and it's part of the retained semantic ("the slot knows its selection"). Also non-CSS renderers (GTK, future) need the selection conveyed to them... actually no—non-CSS renderers measure themselves and pick locally (per spec). FIT_CHANGED is app-<->renderer sync. Keep it.

OK so I think the design is:

**Design: SizeThatFits transmits all candidates as children; HTML renderer gates each in a container-query wrapper; FIT_CHANGED continues for app-side selection state (no TREE swap on the web anymore).**

Let me reconsider whether to keep the child-swap so that non-web renderers and network stay lean. The issue is literally about SSR over network. The simplest, most robust model:

### Option A (recommended): All candidates as children, container-query visibility on the web
- **Protocol/spec change**: `SIZE_THAT_FITS` children = all candidates (N children). `FIT_QUERY` thresholds still riding. The selected index is no longer conveyed by "which child"—the renderer picks via measure/container-query and reports FIT_CHANGED, and the app keeps `fitIndex`. An unchanged fit emits zero opcodes (candidates unchanged). 
  - Hmm, but "only one child on the wire" is a real bandwidth optimization AND the spec in PRIMITIVES.md/LAYOUT.md says children: at most one. Changing it touches: spec (DSL/PRIMITIVES/LAYOUT/OPCODE?), Java FitSlot render + emitter, Rust pathland-view SizeThatFits, TS client, HTML renderer, golden fixtures, conformance vectors.
  - The tradeoff: transmitting every candidate's subtree (background music demo candidates are large-ish: full controls row). But 2 candidates each. Fine.
- **HTML renderer**: slot div becomes a container (`container-type: inline-size`), each candidate wrapped in `<div style="@container ...>`—wait, container queries can't be inline; they need a `<style>` block. Options:
  1. Emit a per-document `<style>` block with `@container (min-width: T_i) { ... }` rules keyed by slot id + candidate index. Generated from FIT_QUERY (thresholds) and candidate count.
  2. Use inline `style` with `display:none !important` overridden by a `<style>` block — still needs a style block.
  - Actually the cleaner approach: each candidate wrapper gets `data-pathland-fit-cand="i"` and we generate container-query rules. Container query needs a `container-type` on the slot and the query uses `@container (min-width: Xpx)`. The bracket ranges: fit rule is `max{ i : thresholds[i] <= width }`. So candidate i is visible when `thresholds[i] <= width < thresholds[i+1]`. Container queries support both min and max: `@container (min-width: T_i) and (max-width: T_{i+1}-1)` but boundaries/float thresholds and "exactly equal picks lower index" matter. Actually since thresholds are floats in logical points, and widths are in css px (which are also logical points-ish at DPR... no, CSS px ARE logical/device-independent). Browser width matches thresholds in px. Boundaries: equal threshold → higher index wins (larger index = higher threshold; but if thresholds equal t==t, lower index wins). Container query ranges can express this but "less than next threshold" for floats: `max-width: T_{i+1}` is inclusive of the boundary, which would wrongly show candidate i at width == T_{i+1}. Need `max-width: T_{i+1} - 0.1px`? Hacky. 

  Hmm. This is where container query ranges get fiddly. But actually container queries support the newer comparison syntax? `@container (width < 640px)` — yes! Modern container queries support range syntax like media queries: `@container (width < 640px)`, `(640px <= width < 1024px)`. Browser support: Chrome 111+, Safari 17+, Firefox 121+ (2023-2024). Reasonable. So:
    - candidate i visible when `thresholds[i] <= width && width < thresholds[i+1]` (with the fit rule's tie-break only complicating equal-threshold duplicates). For the LAST candidate: `width >= thresholds[last]`.
    - equal thresholds: lower index wins → a duplicate band: candidate i with equal threshold as i+1 → only i ever shows (i+1 never). Range for i+1 would be empty. The fit_index rule already handles: for equal thresholds, selected stops at the lower. We can just emit rules that mirror fitIndexFor exactly, including skipping duplicates.
  - So generate per-slot CSS: `@container pl-{slot-id} (width >= T_i) and (width < T_{i+1}) { [data-pathland-id=...] }`. Simpler: candidate wrapper spans. Or apply to the child's own wrapper div with data attribute.

- **TS client**: 
  - Hydrate: candidate wrappers already have correct container queries from SSR's `<style>` block. But the client ALSO needs to emit the style rules when creating slot nodes at runtime (or maintain a `<style data-pathland-fit>` element it updates). Since deltas can create NEW SizeThatFits slots (rare but possible), the client should generate the same CSS. Or simpler: keep the ResizeObserver but instead of toggling display, just report FIT_CHANGED. Visibility handled by container query CSS consistently between SSR+runtime. So client needs to generate/update the style block.
  - Actually, simpler unified approach: the DOM client maintains a `<style data-pathland-fit>` element and writes `@container` rules, regenerated whenever FIT_QUERY changes. On hydrate it re-uses the SSR-generated rules (they're already in the doc). On new slots it adds rules.
  - FIT_CHANGED: still report transitions (via ResizeObserver) so app fitIndex stays in sync. No structural child swap needed anymore (all candidates present). This significantly simplifies the client (no delete/insert of slot children on fit change) AND kills the flash-of-wrong-variant.

- **Java FitSlot**: render all candidates as children. Keep FIT_QUERY. Keep fitInput (FIT_CHANGED sink) updating fitIndex; but structuralContent now returns... all candidates? Actually node.children = all candidates always; fitInput just updates the signal (app logic) — no structural reconcile swap. OR keep structuralContent returning the selected only for non-web renderers? That bifurcates. If the wire always carries all candidates, then GTK (whenever it implements fit) measures and shows one. But GTK fit is deferred. So web is the only fit consumer. Making the wire carry all candidates uniformly is cleanest and future-proof: every renderer receives all candidates and selects locally. That matches statelessness better (renderer picks from what it has).

Wait, but then "renderer must not retain app state" — the slot having all candidates and showing one via CSS: the *visible one* is layout output. Fine.

But there is a real downside: **bandwidth + the "only changes travel" principle**. Candidates that never show still transmit their full subtree on mount and on any internal change. The spec explicitly engineered to avoid this ("the others never transmit"). The user's request is literally to overrule this for first-presentation correctness. I should surface this tradeoff clearly and let the user decide (they already proposed it, so they've accepted it — but I should still note the delta-efficiency implication, e.g. background candidate changes ride the wire while hidden).

Actually re-reading the user: "render all branches of the SizeThatFits and then use css to only render the matching one. The container queries should match the Fit's specified. And then after first render it should hydrate and work with delta changes afterwards."

"work with delta changes afterwards" — I think this means: after the first (SSR) render, the normal delta/hydration flow continues to work (as today). It does NOT necessarily mean "keep the child-swap model". But it COULD mean: SSR renders all (so first paint is correct), but after hydration reconnect to the single-child delta model? That would cause a transition where SSR shows all-candidates and then a full snapshot collapses to one child... which reintroduces the flash. I think the coherent end-state is all-candidates-always (Option A1), and "delta changes afterwards" = normal SET_TEXT/PROPERTY/TREE deltas keep applying to whatever is on screen, FIT_CHANGED keeps the app signal in sync.

Hmm, but actually there's an even lighter-weight interpretation that avoids the wire change:

### Option B: SSR-only — all candidates rendered ONLY in SSR HTML, generated by giving the HTML renderer access to candidates via a separate mechanism
The Rust HTML renderer is a pure function of opcodes. It can't see un-transmitted candidates. The Java server (PathlandSession) authors the app tree — it KNEW all candidates at authoring time (the Java views). It could render the SSR HTML not through the opcode stream but... no, SSR HTML is built by `render_document(opcodes, strings, root)`. To include all candidates, the opcode stream must include them. No way around it without violating the pure-function renderer principle. So the wire change is essentially required by the user's approach. (Alternatively the server could emit a special "SSR probe" frame containing all candidates, but that's a bespoke side-channel — worse.)

So **Option A is the way**. Let me also decide:
- Keep FIT_CHANGED as a real event (transitions on ResizeObserver) — yes, app reads fitIndex. But there's a wrinkle: FIT_CHANGED is host→guest; the guest (app) keeps the canonical fitIndex; the renderer is stateless (doesn't store it — it stores measured width as layout, and "lastIndex" only as a send-coalescing cache, which is allowed as output cache). Fine, unchanged.

But wait: there's an important subtlety about statelessness + container queries. The renderer's *visible* candidate is determined by CSS, not by stored JS state. That's actually MORE stateless than today (today the DOM client computes index in JS from measured width; with container queries the browser computes it). Good for the principle. The DOM client still needs the ResizeObserver ONLY to emit FIT_CHANGED transitions (reporting), not to change visibility. 

Actually — could FIT_CHANGED also be driven by observing which candidate is visible? No, simpler to keep ResizeObserver.

Now, the container-query CSS generation. Where do rules live?
- SSR: the renderer can emit a `<style data-pathland-fit>` block (like the tokens block) containing `@container name (…) { … }` rules. Needs slot container-name uniqueness (id-based) since nested slots.
- The wrapper: candidate children need to be individually selectable. If SizeThatFits has N children, render each child wrapped in a div `data-pathland-fit-cand="i"`. But careful: adding a wrapper changes the layout transparency contract (slot forwards parent's align/justify). Wrapper should be `display: contents` by default, hidden (`display: none`) when not matching → but you can't put `display:none` inside a `display:contents` wrapper's query if the wrapper itself is the gated element. Make the *wrapper* the gated element: default `display:none`, and when its band matches → `display:contents` (so candidates lay out exactly as the slot's flex children, preserving existing alignment behavior). Actually `display:contents` makes the wrapper transparent; the candidate inner element then participates directly in the slot flex layout. That preserves the current "layout transparent" behavior perfectly!
  - So: wrapper `style="display:none"`, container rule `@container pl-{slot} (min-width:T_i) { [data-pathland-id={wrapper}] { display:contents } }`. But the wrapper needs an id for the client to apply deltas to the child inside it. Hmm — if wrapper is a non-node element (not in the tree), the client's runtime renderer doesn't know about wrappers. For deltas that create children of a slot at runtime, the client creates the child element — but where does the wrapper come from?
  - Option: make the wrapper carry the node id and the child be inside without its own id conflict... but child nodes have ids too. Today slot id = div.pathland-ftf, child id = the candidate node. If we add a wrapper per candidate, we need the wrapper and the real element. The DOM client's apply() manipulates elements by `[data-pathland-id]`. We could:
    - wrapper: `data-pathland-id="{childId}"` + class `pathland-ftf-cand` + `display:none` default; and the real child element WITHOUT a data-id (pure content) inside it? But the client looks up elements by id to apply props. If the wrapper has the id, props apply to the wrapper — wrong (they must apply to the innermost element). Unless the wrapper is `display:contents` (transparent) and props applied to it still style it — with display:contents, inherited properties still flow, but properties like width/flex on the wrapper affect layout as if... display:contents element's own box styles apply to the box it "expands" into? Actually with display:contents, the element's box is dropped and descendants render as if they were children of the parent; styles set on the contents element (like width, flex) do NOT apply (no box). So applying node styles to the wrapper is wrong.
    - Better: keep two elements — wrapper div (no id, `pathland-ftf-cand`) and the id-carrying real element inside; wrapper gated by container query; the id element is the actual node. The client needs to know, when it inserts/deletes a slot child, to wrap it. And the SSR needs to produce the same wrapper structure. And when a slot child is deleted (a candidate removed), the client must remove the wrapper.
  
  This is getting complex on the client side. Alternative that avoids client-side wrapper management substantially: 

  **Gate via the child itself using container query + a data attr + generated rules that set `display:none` on all but the match.** But container queries can't target "all children except the matching one" easily without per-child rules. With rules per child using an attribute, yeah we're back to wrappers *or* child-level rules.

  Simpler idea: **put the container query on the slot, and make each candidate a child; emit rules that hide everyone, then show the band.** Each candidate needs a selector. If candidates keep their own element (id = candidate id), the rule can target `[data-pathland-fit-cand="i"]` where we add that attr to the candidate's OWN element at SSR and at runtime-create. But runtime-created children are created generically by element.ts per component — we'd add the cand attr when inserting into a slot as child index. And the rule toggles `display`. But the candidate elements have legit display styles (flex etc.) set inline; a `@container` rule with equal specificity should still win for `display` if we use `!important` or make it a class on the element. Complexity again.

Honestly, the cleanest is wrapper-divs managed on both sides:
- SSR: slot children wrapped in `<div class="pathland-ftf-cand" data-pathland-fit-cand="i">…real child…</div>`, default `display:none`, plus `<style>` with `@container` rules to `display:contents` the matching wrapper. The real child keeps its id.
- Client: when inserting a child under a slot (SIZE_THAT_FITS), wrap it in the same gated div; on delete, remove wrapper. When applying props, apply to the real child (which has the id) — the client's existing `getElementById`/parent lookup still finds the real child (wrapper has no id). 

But hold on — the existing client find logic: `container.querySelector('[data-pathland-id=...]')` and parent traversal. Inserting a child into the slot: the slot's single child currently is attached directly. With wrappers we must target the wrapper as insertion point but apply to inner. The client's apply for `CMD_INSERT_CHILD` / `CMD_ADD_CHILD` picks a reference node by id among the container's existing children (to insert before). With wrapper-divs, the reference elements are still found by their id attributes (real children), and `insertBefore(ref, wrapper)` logic: we need `ref.parentElement` = wrapper. Because wrappers are display:contents, the real child's offsetParent/parentElement is the wrapper. `insertBefore` on the slot container with a wrapper `ref.parentElement` works. Doable but fiddly.

Given the scope, I think the plan should present the architecture and decompose into concrete steps, and explicitly call out the wrapper strategy and the CSS generation (style block, container-name, range syntax), plus the spec updates and test updates, and let the user confirm the key semantic changes:
1. Wire change: slot transmits all candidates (children = N). (Confirmed by user's proposal.)
2. FIT_CHANGED remains, no child swap on web (all candidates present); keep signal for app state.
3. Delta-efficiency tradeoff (background candidates' changes ride the wire) — acceptable for correctness.

Let me also double check whether there's an alternative: keep sending 1 child but have SSR render all by having the EMITTER, for the SSR document build, emit all candidates. But the emitter is the same for SSR and live; no separate code path. So no.

Also consider: what about renderers without container-query support (SSR conformance html-golden; and GTK is out of scope). The SSR HTML itself only needs CSS; the html-golden fixtures would change to include wrappers+style.

Also FIT_CHANGED cadence: "reports only on transitions" — the DOM client ResizeObserver cadence is unchanged.

Let me also think: does the app still need the child-swap AT ALL in the all-candidates model? The Java FitSlot's structuralContent renders all candidates; the emitter no longer swaps. But the Java `FitSlot` uses `fitSelection` to... only for its own render? If we always render all, `structuralContent` returns all candidates. `node.fitSelection` / `restoreFitSelection` logic becomes obsolete on the web but might still be useful to keep the signal correct. Actually since children are now all candidates always, restore-fit-selection no longer applies. The Rust DSL `fit_index` field also becomes vestigial (it selects which subset to emit — now emits all). We keep the fields but stop gating emission, OR keep gating for NON-web renderers? Statelessness says renderer decides; app just provides candidates + thresholds. Cleanest: emit all, always. The Java fitIndex signal still updates from FIT_CHANGED (app can read current fit for effects) — keep that.

But one more subtlety: the spec says before first measure the app renders index 0. With all candidates present, "index 0 shown" happens automatically via container query at width < first real threshold OR if no thresholds, all plus width>=... hmm: candidate 0 has minWidth 0; container query `width < T_1` shows 0; else 1. If thresholds are [0, 640]: 0 shows when `0 <= width < 640` → "compact" style. Equivalent. Good.

Now, is there a risk that container queries with `display:contents` inside a flex slot where the slot is `display:flex; flex-direction:inherit` etc. — the candidate becomes a flex item of the slot (as today) when its wrapper is contents. 

Also: `container-type: inline-size` on the slot. Today slot is `display:flex; ...; flex:1 1 auto`. Adding `container-type: inline-size` (and `container-name: pl-{id}`) makes it a size container. Its own width = filled width (good, that's the measuring unit). Container query reads its width. 

Edge: `container-type: size` requires explicit dimensions? `inline-size` only requires inline size be non-auto — slot has `flex:1 1 auto` so it fills. Good.

Also SSR style block: generated per document in render_document head (like token_style). And the DOM client, for runtime-created slots, must add the same rules — maintain a `<style data-pathland-fit>` element and append rules for each slot id + FIT_QUERY change. Regenerate on data-pathland-fit change (FIT_QUERY SET_PROPERTY). 

This is a substantial but well-scoped change. Let me now also verify browser support note: container query range syntax `(width >= 640px)` and `(width < 1024px)` — supported baseline 2023. Also could avoid range syntax by emitting two-part min/max with `and`. Range is cleaner. I'll mention using `min-width`/`max-width` with `and` as fallback-safe (better support): `@container pl-2 (min-width: 640px) and (max-width: 1023px)` but floats/equal-threshold... equal thresholds handled by skipping duplicate bands. Boundary inclusivity: `max-width: T_{i+1}` includes T_{i+1} — at exactly T_{i+1}, both i and i+1 match → ambiguity. fitIndexFor: thresholds[i] <= width, so at width == T_{i+1}, index i+1 wins (higher index). CSS with `min-width: T_{i+1}` and i's rule `max-width: T_{i+1}` both true → both visible. Need to avoid: use `max-width: < T_{i+1}`? CSS has `(width < 640px)` range syntax which is strict — perfect for the fit rule. So use strict-comparison range syntax: candidate i: `@container (width >= T_i) and (width < T_{i+1})`; last: `(width >= T_last)`. First candidate threshold 0: `(width >= 0) and (width < T_1)`. For equal thresholds duplicate skip: if T_i == T_{i+1}, the range for i covers [T_i, T_i) empty → never shows; i+1 would be [T_i,...) but fitIndexFor picks lower index → i+1 never shows either! Equal thresholds: fit rule "equal thresholds pick the lower index" means only the FIRST with that threshold ever selected; later duplicates are unreachable. So skip generating rules for duplicate thresholds after the first occurrence (i.e., candidate j with T_j == T_{j-1} gets an empty/never rule). Fine — generate rules only for "selectable" candidates, others `display:none` always.

OK the design is solid. Let me write the plan with phases, touching exact files. I should present it and ask a couple of clarifying decisions:
1. Confirm wire change to always transmit all candidates (bandwidth tradeoff) — the user already proposed it, but I want to confirm the delta-efficiency consequence is acceptable. Possibly offer a refinement: emit all candidates, but this is a protocol change (version bump note).
2. Whether the DOM client should keep ResizeObserver for FIT_CHANGED (yes) — probably no need to ask.
3. Spec update scope: PRIMITIVES.md, LAYOUT.md, DSL.md, OPCODE.md?, EVENTS.md — update "children: at most one" language.

I'll present the plan with the architecture, phases, files, tests, and ask focused questions. Since this is plan mode, I present and await approval; I'll include the questions inline.

Let me quickly check the Java emitter reconcileSlot and FitSlot to know the file/line scope for the plan, and the pathland-html-golden + conformance vector for 28a to note updates. I already have enough from the exploration for those references. Let me also check whether there's an existing `<style data-pathland-fit>` concept or container usage in TS apply.ts / index.ts / classes. Quick grep.
I have the complete picture. Let me do a couple of final checks on the client-side style handling and the conformance vector, then present the plan.

parts.text:
Now I have a complete understanding. Let me think about the design carefully.

## The problem

Issue #141: over network, `SizeThatFits` may delay the first correct rendering. Currently:
- The wire only carries the **selected** child (one child).
- SSR renders that single (default index-0 = fallback) child.
- Client measures its width, derives fit, reports `FIT_CHANGED`, server swaps → second frame correct.

So over network the first paint may show the smallest/fallback candidate even when the real slot is wide, then corrects after a round trip.

## The user's proposal

Render **all** branches (all candidates) in the SSR HTML, and use **CSS container queries** that match the Fit's `minWidth` thresholds so the browser shows only the matching candidate on first paint. After that, hydrate and rely on the delta flow (FIT_CHANGED → server swaps the transmitted child).

## Key architectural implications

1. **The wire today carries one child.** To render all branches SSR-side, either:
   - **A: change the protocol** so `SIZE_THAT_FITS` transmits all candidates as children (then the renderer picks via container queries), OR
   - **B: keep one child on wire, but SSR has access to all candidates through some other channel.**

Since the Rust HTML renderer is a pure function of the opcode stream, and the JS client only has what reached it, "SSR renders all branches" requires the candidates to be available to the SSR renderer. The clean way consistent with the architecture: **the emitter transmits all candidates as children**, and the `FIT_CHANGED` flow becomes... wait. But then who picks? The renderer picks via container query (CSS). Then FIT_CHANGED would still be reported but the server's child-swap becomes unnecessary — the renderer already has all children and just toggles visibility.

That's a real semantic shift: today "renderer is stateless; app owns tree; app swaps the child." If all candidates ride the wire and the DOM client toggles visibility via CSS container queries (no server round trip needed), then FIT_CHANGED becomes merely informational (or could be dropped / kept for app logic like analytics or if the app wants the index).

But wait — the user said: "And then after first render it should hydrate and work with delta changes afterwards." So they want: first presentation correct via CSS; afterwards the normal delta/swap flow continues. That suggests a **hybrid**:
- SSR HTML contains ALL candidates, each wrapped in a container-query-gated element.
- On hydration, the client picks up where SSR left off. The client keeps all candidates in DOM, and uses container queries to show the right one. FIT_CHANGED is still sent so the app knows; and the server's delta child-swap... hmm.

There's tension. Let me think about the two coherent end-states:

### Option 1: Full "renderer owns all candidates" model
- Protocol: `SIZE_THAT_FITS` node's **children are all candidates** (sorted ascending), plus `FIT_QUERY` thresholds. Wire carries all of them.
- The renderer (web) shows the matching one via container query; CSS toggles visibility.
- `FIT_CHANGED` still emitted (host→guest) so the app's retained index stays in sync, but no child-swap deltas are needed from the app (all children are already there). The renderer is still stateless in the sense that it renders all transmitted children and shows the one matching its measured width (output selection is layout, not retained app state — the measurement is layout output).
- Pros: first paint correct (CSS), no round-trip to correct. Simple, one mechanism.
- Cons: **bandwidth** — all candidates' subtrees always travel, not just the selected one. This reverses the original design intent ("only the selected child transmits"). For a server-rendered UI with small candidates this is fine, but it's a protocol/spec change with a real (if small) cost: every fit-slot transmits all its branches. Also more complexity in the emitter (always emit all children, not one).

Worse: **contradicts "only changes travel" and the whole point of the slot**. But actually if candidates rarely change it's not a big deal.

Hmm, but there's an even simpler reading: maybe keep the wire as-is (one selected child for the *live* delta model), but for **SSR only**, the server renders all branches. How would SSR get all branches? The SSR renderer (`render_document` in Rust HTML) is fed the opcode stream. If the stream only has one child, it can't render the others. UNLESS the app, when building the SSR document, emits a "preview" super-set. That's hacky and violates the pure-function-of-opcode-stream principle.

So the honest conclusion: to render all branches in SSR, the candidates must be on the wire. That's Option 1.

That's complex, stateful in the client (must reconcile "SSR had N children, deltas now swap to 1"), and re-introduces a window where the DOM has stale branches. Not clean.

### Option 3: Container queries drive visibility on the LIVE DOM too, but FIT_CHANGED still reports index; app stops swapping children; all candidates stay on wire permanently.
Same as Option 1 really. This is the cleanest.

The **spirit** of statelessness + the existing mechanism: the client reports FIT_CHANGED on band-crossing; if all candidates are on the wire, the client CAN just toggle which one is visible WITHOUT needing a server swap at all. But should it? Two sub-options:

Each candidate child is wrapped in a `<div data-cand="i">` (or class) with rules like `@container (min-width: Ni)` — but container queries can't be inline... Now I understand the full picture. The SSR emits a fragment via `pathland_html_render` (or `render_fragment`), which is embedded into a document with the built-in `<style>` block + token styles in `<head>`. So for container queries, we need a `<style>` element or the built-in CSS to include container-query rules.

Container queries cannot be expressed inline in `style=` attributes — they must be in a stylesheet (`@container` at-rules). So the approach needs to generate a `<style>` block per document with `@container` rules keyed to the slot's `data-pathland-id`.

Let me now think about the design carefully.

## The proposal

"Render all branches of SizeThatFits, use CSS container queries to show the matching one, hydrate after first render and work with delta changes afterwards."

### Current behavior
- Wire carries one child (the selected candidate).
- SSR renders that single child.
- DOM client measures → reports FIT_CHANGED → server swaps → deltas.

### Proposed behavior
- **SSR emits ALL candidates** as children of the fit slot. Each candidate is wrapped in a `<div data-pathland-fit-cand="i">` (or similar) with a CSS class.
- The slot `<div class="pathland-ftf">` gets `container-type: inline-size` (and maybe `container-name`) so it becomes a container query root.
- A `<style>` block (or the built-in CSS) carries `@container` rules keyed on the slot id: `@container (min-width: 0px) and (max-width: 639px) { ... show candidate 0, hide 1 }`, `@container (min-width: 640px) { ... show candidate 1, hide 0 }`. Only the matching candidate is visible on first paint — correct SSR without a round trip.
- On live (web client): the same structure stays — all candidates present, CSS container queries pick visibility, ResizeObserver... **does the client still send FIT_CHANGED?**

This is the crux. With all candidates present, the renderer no longer needs the server to swap the child — CSS does it locally. So:
- Option A: Keep FIT_CHANGED flow for app-side state (the app still wants to know the fit index for its own logic), but the *child swap* is no longer needed because all candidates are there. The emitter keeps emitting all candidates always.
- Option B: FIT_CHANGED is dropped entirely; the renderer is fully local; app never knows the fit.

But statelessness principle: the renderer must not retain app state. The server owns the tree. In the new model, the server transmits all candidates; the renderer shows the matching one. The renderer's "selection" is layout output (which it measures), not retained app state — that's fine and matches how the current client already derives fit locally.

But should FIT_CHANGED still flow? Consider: the app might want to react to the fit (e.g. its own logic, or the `fitIndex` signal in Java DSL, or analytics). Also non-web renderers (GTK) don't support CSS container queries — they measure and pick, and report FIT_CHANGED. Keeping FIT_CHANGED as the cross-renderer contract is clean: the renderer *reports* the derived index; the app may ignore it or use it. But the current protocol semantics are "the app swaps in response." If we keep all candidates on the wire, the swap becomes a no-op (the app re-emitting a subtree that's all present). 

Hmm, let me think about what "work with delta changes afterwards" means for the user:
- First render: all candidates, CSS picks. ✓
- After hydration: the live delta flow continues to work. That means: SET_TEXT/PARAMETER/TREE deltas for anything that changes; FIT_CHANGED still reported and the app can still react.

The simplest consistent design that satisfies "first presentation correct + then deltas work":

**Always transmit all candidates** (FIT_QUERY + all candidate children). The web renderer renders each candidate in a container-query gated wrapper. FIT_CHANGED is still emitted by the client's ResizeObserver on transitions so the app's `fitIndex` signal stays in sync (and non-web renderers can use it). The emitter in the Java DSL keeps emitting all candidates as children; `structuralContent` returns all candidates instead of one. The `fitInput` on the node updates the `fitIndex` signal (app-side state) but no child swap is needed.

Wait — but then what about "the app swaps the slot's child" contract? With all candidates transmitted, swapping is unnecessary. But keeping FIT_CHANGED (host→guest) means the app still learns the index. The reverse — the app emitting a child swap — becomes redundant for web. But other renderers (GTK) might still rely on the single-child contract... but GTK doesn't implement fit at all yet (deferred). So actually changing the contract for everyone is fine.

Actually, let me reconsider. There's risk of a big change. Let me consider a *minimal* design that keeps the existing single-child wire contract and only changes SSR:

### Minimal: SSR-only "all candidates" via the renderer, wire unchanged
The problem: the wire carries one child. SSR needs all candidates. Where do candidates come from at SSR time? They're in the app's retained views (Java DSL renders the app tree). But SSR = Rust renderer fed by the opcode stream. The candidates must be IN the opcode stream for the Rust renderer to render them. So we can't render all candidates SSR-side without transmitting them.

Unless... the app emits them specifically for the first frame. E.g., the emitter, on first emission, emits ALL candidates as children of the fit slot, and on FIT_CHANGED-driven re-emit, emits only the selected. That's stateful/awkward and breaks the "only one child" decode invariant.

So the clean way truly requires the node to carry all candidates. This is the crux: **the protocol must carry all fit candidates as children.** Then:
- SSR renders all candidates, gated by container queries → first paint correct. ✓
- Web client shows/hides via container queries; ResizeObserver reports FIT_CHANGED transitions so app signal syncs. ✓
- Deltas afterwards work: any candidate's content changes ride normal SET_TEXT/PARAMETER/TREE deltas; a candidate added/removed rides TREE deltas. ✓
- The app no longer swaps children on FIT_CHANGED (they're all present); FIT_CHANGED is informational/sync.

This changes:
1. Spec: PRIMITIVES.md / LAYOUT.md / DSL.md / EVENTS.md — "children: at most one" → "children: all candidates"; FIT_CHANGED semantics: "reported so the app's fitIndex stays in sync; the app does not swap (all candidates are transmitted)". I have a good picture now. Let me think through the design carefully before presenting the plan.

## Key architectural facts

1. **Wire today**: `SIZE_THAT_FITS` carries exactly ONE child (the selected candidate). The app (Java/or Rust DSL) owns candidates; only the selected one transmits. `FIT_CHANGED` (host→guest) reports the derived index so the app swaps the transmitted child.

2. **The user's proposal**: render ALL branches in SSR, use CSS container queries to pick the matching one on first paint, then hydrate and use deltas afterwards.

3. **The fundamental constraint**: The Rust HTML renderer is a *pure function of the opcode stream*. It can only render what reaches it. If the wire only carries one child, SSR cannot possibly render all branches. So the candidates must reach the renderer somehow.

Two ways to get all branches to SSR:
- **A. Change the wire/protocol**: `SIZE_THAT_FITS` transmits ALL candidates as children (a real change to "children: at most one"). Then the emitter sends all, SSR renders all wrapped in container-query gated divs, CSS picks the match on first paint, hydrate keeps them, and FIT_CHANGED still flows (host→guest) to keep the app's retained index in sync — but the renderer no longer needs the server to swap (visibility is CSS-pure). Actually with all candidates present, the renderer can pick locally via CSS; FIT_CHANGED becomes mostly informational (app-side signal). This is a real protocol change affecting PRIMITIVES.md, LAYOUT.md, EVENTS.md, the emitters (Java FitSlot, Rust engine), TS client logic, conformance vectors.

- **B. Keep wire as-is (one child), and give SSR the candidate set via a side channel**. But that violates the "renderer is pure function of opcode stream" principle and adds a parallel path — messy, non-idiomatic.

So the natural reading of the user's request is A: emit all candidates, render all in SSR gated by container queries, first paint correct, then hydrate/deltas. The "after first render it should hydrate and work with delta changes afterwards" tells us: after the SSR (no-JS first paint done right via CSS), the existing delta machinery continues — FIT_CHANGED still reported, app still swaps the transmitted child (or keeps all children present and the client just toggles visibility).

Wait — there's tension: with A, do we keep "children: at most one" on the wire and only have SSR emit all (a first-frame-only superset)? Or always emit all?

Let me reconsider the user's exact words: "So render all branches of the SizeThatFits and then use css to only render the matching one." — "render all branches" in the SSR HTML. "The container queries should match the Fit's specified." — CSS container queries keyed to the minWidth thresholds. "And then after first render it should hydrate and work with delta changes afterwards." — after the initial SSR paint, hydration + the normal delta flow (FIT_CHANGED → app swaps single transmitted child) resumes.

The cleanest interpretation that preserves the protocol's "only changes travel" and keeps FIT_CHANGED meaningful: 

**The SSR frame (initial full render) transmits ALL candidates** so the HTML renderer can render all branches. Then the app continues with its normal single-selected-child model: FIT_CHANGED arrives, the app swaps the transmitted child, and the renderer applies TREE deltas. But wait — if the DOM already contains all candidates wrapped in container-query gates, and then a TREE delta removes 3 and inserts 1 (the swap), the pretty container-query setup would be destroyed by the delta application... unless the delta client keeps all candidates and just toggles CSS.

Hmm. There are really two coherent end-states:

**Design X — "renderer keeps all candidates forever, CSS is the selector":**
- Wire: `SIZE_THAT_FITS` always carries ALL candidates as children (sorted ascending + FIT_QUERY). 
- Renderer (web): renders every candidate in a `<div data-fit-cand="i">` gated by a `@container` query tied to the slot's thresholds. Visibility is pure CSS — first paint correct with zero JS.
- FIT_CHANGED (host→guest) still emitted on transitions so the app's retained `fitIndex` signal stays correct (for app logic / other renderers), but the web renderer does NOT need the app to swap children — it has all of them.
- Delta changes afterwards: a candidate's content changes ride normal `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`/`TREE` deltas; adding/removing candidates rides `TREE` deltas (client re-gates). An unchanged fit = zero opcodes. FIT_CHANGED becomes a *sync* event, not a *structural request*.
- Pros: single mechanism, first paint correct, resize is zero-latency pure CSS (no round-trip even on resize!). 
- Cons: **breaks the "only the selected child transmits" bandwidth optimization** — all candidates always transmit. For small candidates that's fine, but it reverses an explicit spec decision ("only changes travel", "the others never transmit"). Also changes FIT_CHANGED semantics (no structural swap needed).

**Design Y — "SSR-only superset; live stays one-child":**
- Wire: unchanged (one selected child). But for SSR, the emitter is told to emit ALL candidates *for the first frame* (a special initial snapshot) ... but that's still transmitting them, and after connect the client has all branches in DOM but the delta stream assumes one child → the swap delta would delete the superset. Messy: you'd need the client to reconcile (drop container gates once the single-child model takes over). Essentially "SSR renders all for correct first paint, then on live connect the DOM devolves to the single-child model". That's the "hydrate and work with delta changes afterwards" reading — SSR full, then live single. But then on first live connect, if the measured fit differs from the SSR-picked one, there's a flicker: SSR shows wide (CSS), then FIT_CHANGED→swap→now compact. Actually no: the DOM client on connect keeps the SSR HTML; the fit is measured client-side; if it matches, zero opcodes; only a mismatch swaps. But if the client devolved to single-child, the container-query gates must be torn down.

Design Y has a serious problem: the wire carries (initially) all candidates but the protocol says one child. The emitter would have to knowingly over-emit at boot then correct — but the *app's retained tree* has all candidates; emitting all at boot is actually truthful (the app does own all candidates).

Hmm, actually, I think the user's mental model is simpler and cleaner than either X or Y as I've framed them. Let me re-read once more:

"render all branches of the SizeThatFits and then use css to only render the matching one. The container queries should match the Fit's specified. And then after first render it should hydrate and work with delta changes afterwards."

I think the spirit is: **first presentation (SSR) renders all; CSS container queries pick immediately, no network needed for a correct first paint. Then the existing delta/hydration model continues to work** (i.e., we don't break the live delta flow; FIT_CHANGED still flows, the app still can swap, content updates still apply).

The design question that genuinely needs the user's input:
1. Do we change the wire to **always carry all candidates** (Design X — CSS as the permanent selector, fd FIT_CHANGED purely informational on web), OR
2. **SSR-only superset**: emit all candidates **only for the SSR/initial frame**, keep the live single-child + FIT_CHANGED-swap model (Design Y)? 

Both have real tradeoffs. This is exactly the kind of decision I should surface to the user.

Actually, wait. Let me reconsider the architecture of SSR more concretely to see if there's an even simpler path that doesn't require a wire change at all.

SSR pipeline: Java app → FrameOpcodeSink emits one self-contained frame → HtmlRenderer (JNA) → `pathland_html_render(batch, root)` → Rust decode → render_node → fragment. Then PathlandSession wraps into a document. The TOKENS/STYLE `<style>` blocks come from render_document (Rust) — but the SSR path uses the fragment + a pre-built shell. Wait, the Java SSR calls `renderer.render(sink.frame(), rootId)` which is `pathland_html_render` (not `_fragment`?). Let me check — `pathland_html_render` calls render_fragment or render_document? From capi.rs, `pathland_html_render` returns... let me recall the shim: `Pointer pathland_html_render(Pointer batch, int len, int root)`. I should verify which Rust fn it binds to.

Actually this matters for where the container-query `<style>` rules go. If render_document, the Rust renderer can inject a `<style data-pathland-fit>` block in head with per-slot `@container` rules. If render_fragment, rules must ride inline or a preceding `<style>` in the document shell.

Given the Java layer calls `pathland_html_render` (not `_fragment`), and capi.rs `pathland_html_render` likely = render_document (since `_fragment` exists separately). Let me confirm quickly in the plan-research step. I already grepped: capi.rs line 52 `pathland_html_render` and line 59 `pathland_html_render_fragment`. The Java shim uses `pathland_html_render`. In the Rust tests, `pathland_html_render`'s test at capi.rs:150 renders with `render_document`? Not sure. I'll confirm during research but it's a detail for implementation.

Now the CRITICAL decision I must put to the user. Let me also weigh:

The cleanest, most "Pathland" answer: since the renderer is *pure* and *stateless*, and CSS is a *pure renderer-side* selection, **Design X (always transmit all candidates; CSS selects; resize needs zero wire)** is architecturally the most consistent. It actually *improves* the resize story (no latency at all) and removes the round-trip the issue complains about. The cost is bandwidth (all candidates always) and a spec change to FIT_CHANGED meaning.

Design Y preserves bandwidth but keeps a two-model world (SSR all / live one) with teardown complexity — and ironically reintroduces the very round-trip latency (resize → FIT_CHANGED → swap) the issue wants to fix.

I lean strongly to X. But I should present this to the user because it reverses an explicit, much-emphasized spec decision ("the others never transmit", "only changes travel", FIT_CHANGED's structural role). The user may care about preserving the single-child wire.

Let me also think about whether X actually needs FIT_CHANGED at all on web. With all candidates present and CSS selecting, the web renderer never reports structurally. But the app (Java) keeps a `fitIndex` signal that also gates nothing on the web... but other renderers (GTK, future) and the app's own logic might read it. Keep FIT_CHANGED as a *report* (host→guest) so the app's signal stays live; it's cheap and keeps `fitInput`/state coherent across renderers. Actually with X, is FIT_CHANGED needed? The app signal would otherwise be stale. Yes, keep it — but it no longer drives a swap; it just updates app state. That's still "the renderer selects locally, reports." It matches the existing spec language mostly. Good.

There's also the deterministic-first-render concern: SSR must render the *matching* candidate visibly... but CSS handles it at the browser. The SSR HTML just contains all + gates. The `data-pathland-fit` attr already exists; the SSR could also add a `container-type: inline-size` and per-candidate `@container` — actually the thresholds come from `FIT_QUERY` which SSR already decodes. 

Now container queries: `@container (min-width: 640px)` etc. But the fit rule is bands: candidate i visible when `T_i <= width < T_{i+1}`. Container queries support range syntax like `@container (width >= 640px) and (width < 1024px)`. But exact floats and the "equal thresholds take lower index" rule need care. Also container queries must be in a `<style>` block, not inline. And they consult the *nearest ancestor container* — so the slot div needs `container-type: inline-size`. Children wrapped in `[data-fit-cand]` divs with rules keyed to a container name. Since multiple fit slots can exist, use `container-name` unique per slot (e.g. `pl-ftf-{id}`).

Fallback: browsers without container-query support show candidate 0 (fallback) — the degrades to today's behavior, fine.

TS client: on hydrate it must NOT tear down the SSR all-branch DOM. On live change it must add/remove candidate divs and their gate rules (a `<style data-pathland-fit>` managed element like tokens). The current client's `applyFitQuery` measures and toggles `display`? No—it just reports. Client already doesn't swap; the server swaps. Under X, client only manages gates + reports FIT_CHANGED transitions; insert/remove candidate updates gates.

Also `data-pathland-id` on candidate wrappers: wrappers are new non-node elements. The nodes (candidates) are the children with ids. The wrapper divs are structural, must survive hydrate (Rust emits them, JS hydrates same structure) and be managed on insert/remove (JS must know a SIZE_THAT_FITS parent wraps children). That mirrors the existing "media wrapper" special-case (`mediaToWrapper`) — precedent exists for the client morphing/wrapping children for component-specific structure. Good.

OK. I have enough to present a plan. Let me also confirm which Rust renderer fn Java SSR uses and whether the document-level `<style>` is available, then write the plan and ask the 1 key design question (X vs Y), plus maybe fit-banding edge (equal thresholds).

/// Map a component type to its native widget kind.
pub fn widget_kind(component_type: u16) -> WidgetKind {
    match component_type {
        component_type::VSTACK
        | component_type::HSTACK
        | component_type::LAZY_VSTACK
        | component_type::LAZY_HSTACK => WidgetKind::Stack,
        component_type::TEXT => WidgetKind::Text,
        component_type::BUTTON => WidgetKind::Button,
        component_type::GRID
        | component_type::LAZY_VGRID
        | component_type::LAZY_HGRID => WidgetKind::Grid,

I now have a clear design for the Java side. The key insight:

- `Emitter` is in `com.pathland.view.emit`, `FitSlot` is in `com.pathland.view` (package-private).
- I need a way for `FitSlot.render` to know whether the emitter is doing a **full/snapshot emission** (mount + renderFull) vs a live delta emission (reconcile).
- `mount()` calls `root.render(env)` and then `emitNode(tree)`. The `renderFull()` calls `emitNode(tree)` on the retained tree (not re-render). So the snapshot children are determined at `render` time — but `renderFull` doesn't re-render.

Wait, that's important. `renderFull()` re-emits the *retained tree* — it does NOT re-render the views. So the fit slot children are whatever `FitSlot.render` produced at mount. If mount renders all candidates, the retained tree has all candidates as children, and `renderFull` will re-emit all of them too. That's exactly what we want for A2 (snapshot = mount full frame + resync full frame both carry all candidates).

But the concern: the retained tree holds ALL candidates as children. When a live FIT_CHANGED arrives and the app swaps selection, `reconcileSlot` computes `fresh` = one selected child and diffs against `oldChildren` = all candidates. That would emit REMOVE for the other candidates → N→1 downgrade. That's the A2 behavior we want! Great.

But wait — there's subtlety. If we ALWAYS emit all candidates at mount (into the retained tree), then EVERY emitter (including the GTK Java demo, Rust ring) would carry all candidates. But the GTK Java demo uses the Java DSL too — it mounts the same `MusicPlayerView` via `pathland_gtk_run_ring`. If FitSlot always emits all candidates, the GTK demo's FIT slot would also carry N children — but GTK maps SIZE_THAT_FITS to blank anyway, so no regression there.

But the requirement is: **live emission stays one-child + FIT_CHANGED swap**. If at mount we put all candidates into `node.children`, then:
- mount full frame: all candidates ✓ (SSR gets them)
- live FIT_CHANGED: `reconcileSlot` swaps `structuralContent` (one selected) → diffs all-vs-one → emits REMOVE/delete for the others → N→1 downgrade ✓ (this IS the "after hydration works with deltas" behavior)

Actually wait — this is exactly the right model! The retained tree at mount has all candidates. On the first FIT_CHANGED that actually changes selection, the emitter downgrades to one child. If the width maps to index 0 (the default/fallback), `fitIndex` stays 0, `structuralContent` returns the same view, reconcile emits ZERO opcodes, and the retained tree keeps all candidates. Good.

But here's a problem: at mount, does `reconcileSlot` even run at all? No — `registerBindings` creates a structural effect that calls `reconcileSlot` on signal change. At mount the effect's first run reads the current value without emitting. So if nothing changes, no downgrade. If FIT_CHANGED(0) arrives (width<640, index 0), `fitIndex.set(0)` — equal, signal suppresses → no effect re-run → zero opcodes → tree keeps all candidates. 

Now the question: do we want the live tree to keep ALL candidates forever (until a selection actually changes)? Per A2: "one selected child after FIT_CHANGED". If FIT_CHANGED reports index 0 and the app was already at 0, no downgrade happens — the tree keeps all candidates. Is that OK? The client already hydrated all candidates and the container query handles visibility. That's actually ideal: the container query keeps picking forever, and FIT_CHANGED only matters when the selection *changes* from the app's perspective. But if selection is 0 and stays 0, the app never "selects" anything different, so keeping all candidates is fine and even desirable (first paint correct forever via CSS).

Hmm, but there's a subtlety: if FIT_CHANGED reports index 1, `fitIndex.set(1)` → effect re-runs → `reconcileSlot` computes fresh = selectedView() (index 1 candidate) → `newChildren = [cand1], oldChildren = [cand0, cand1, ...]`. Depending on FIT_QUERY ordering, cand1 might be at position 1 in oldChildren. reconcileChildren diffs by position: position 0 old=cand0 vs fresh=cand1 (different components likely) → delete cand0, create cand1 at index 0... wait let me think about positioning.

Actually `reconcileChildren(parent, oldList, newList, ops)` — oldList is all candidates, newList is [single selected]. Position 0: old=cand0, fresh=selected. If selected is cand1 (different component), it removes cand0, creates selected at index 0. Position 1: old=cand1 (component of cand1) vs fresh=null → remove. Etc. So all old candidates get removed except... actually position 0 removes cand0 and creates fresh; then positions 1..n remove cand1..candN. Final: single child = the selected candidate at position 0. Correct N→1 downgrade. 

If selected IS cand0 (index 0): position 0 old=cand0 vs fresh=cand0 same component → reconcileNode (might be zero-op), positions 1.. remove cand1..N. Downgrade to cand0 single. So even a FIT_CHANGED(0) after mount would downgrade IF the effect runs. But FIT_CHANGED(0) when fitIndex already 0 → suppressed → no downgrade. That's the "SSR keeps all candidates + CSS forever" path, which is fine.

OK so the design for Java:
1. `Emitter`: a package-private mechanism to tell `FitSlot.render` "this is a snapshot emission" so it emits all candidates into `node.children`.
2. But `FitSlot.render` runs during `root.render(env)` at mount — that's ONE call, building the retained tree. There's no second renderFull re-render. So if we make `FitSlot.render` always emit all candidates, the retained tree always has all candidates, and renderFull re-emits them all. That perfectly matches A2 with zero mode-flipping complexity!

Wait — is that true? Let me re-check: does mount re-render the tree on submit? No. `mount` renders once. `renderFull` replays the retained tree. Live deltas via structural effects. So "FitSlot always emits all candidates" = retained tree always has all = snapshot frames (mount + resync) carry all, live reconcile downgrades on selection change. That IS the A2 behavior, achieved purely by changing `FitSlot.render` to add all candidates, no emitter flag needed!

But hold on — does this change the LIVE behavior for the GTK ring / Java GTK demo? At mount, GTK-based Java demo also gets all candidates now. But GTK painter maps SIZE_THAT_FITS → blank, ignores children. So visually no change. But the retained tree in the GTK path also has all candidates... GTK ignores them. OK.

But actually the plan said an explicit "snapshotEmission" flag to keep live byte-identical. If FitSlot always emits all candidates at mount, the FIRST frame (mount) always has all candidates — that's the SSR + GTK-demo mount frame. The GTK demo doesn't SSR; it mounts to a ring. The GTK renderer opens the ring and reads the mount frame. It would now see N children under a fit slot that it maps to blank — ignored. Fine.

Hmm, but do we want "always all candidates at mount" to be unconditional? The user said "invisible to the developer using the DSL" and chose "Option 1: internal emit mode (recommended)" — which describes a flag for full/snapshot emission. But given renderFull doesn't re-render, "full emission" == "the retained tree as built at mount" == "all candidates at mount." So the simplest correct implementation: FitSlot.render emits all candidates into node.children (no flag at all). renderFull re-emits them (snapshot). Live FIT_CHANGED downgrades.

But wait — there's a subtlety with `structuralContent`. Currently `node.structuralContent = () -> selectedView()`. That's used by reconcileSlot to compute the single fresh child. If we keep structuralContent = selectedView, reconcileSlot will downgrade on selection change. Good.

However, there's `restoreFitSelection` at reconcileChildren lines 468-471: nested fit slots carrying selection across a parent-subtree re-render. Since children now include ALL candidates... `fresh.structuralContent != null && old.structuralContent != null` — restoreFitSelection(old, fresh) applies old.fitSelection to fresh. This should still work.

Also `emitSubtreeInto` (used when inserting a fresh child) emits one child. But at mount, `emitNode(tree)` handles the whole tree including multiple children. Fine.

Now the question: do we need an explicit flag at all? Let me reconsider the plan to keep it minimal and safe. The plan (locked) says: "Emitter: package-private field snapshotEmission... Set it during mount's first full frame and renderFull(); leave it off for live endFrame reconcile paths." And "FitSlot.render: when the emitter is in snapshot mode, add every candidate..."

But FitSlot.render is only called at build time (mount), once. It isn't called during reconcile (reconcile uses structuralContent.get() → selectedView().render). So a flag on the emitter consulted by FitSlot.render would ONLY ever be true/false at that one mount call. If we make it true for the mount emission, FitSlot always sees true → always all candidates. So the flag is functionally equivalent to "always emit all candidates" for the retained tree. The only reason to have a flag: if we wanted renderFull to differ from mount, or to keep the GTK ring mount single-child. But GTK ignores fit children anyway.

Hmm, but there's an important consideration: pathland-demo-views `MusicPlayerViewTest` and `SizeThatFitsTest` assert only one child is emitted at mount. Those tests would now see all candidates at mount. That's a deliberate behavior change to TEST — the plan says update SizeThatFitsTest: "assert all candidates emit in an explicitly-snapshot emitter, one child otherwise." That implies the flag approach where default (non-snapshot) emitters still emit one child.

So the flag IS wanted for testability/controllability: a non-snapshot emitter (unit tests, GTK ring?) keeps one child; a snapshot emitter (SSR session) emits all. Let me implement the flag properly:

- `Emitter` gets `boolean snapshotEmission` (package-private field) + `void snapshotEmission(boolean)` or a constructor? PathlandSession constructs the emitter then mounts. `new Emitter(sink, theme)`. Add package-private setter `emitter.withSnapshotEmission(true)`? Or a public method? It's between pathland-server-core and pathland-view — both are separate Maven modules. server-core calls `new Emitter(sink, app.theme())`. For server-core to enable it, the flag must be settable from server-core — that REQUIRES a public (or at least cross-module visible) API. Hmm, that's a public API change!

Wait: "public DSL API byte-identical". A new method on Emitter is technically public API but NOT the DSL authoring surface (Emitter is internal plumbing in com.pathland.view.emit, not View/SizeThatFits/Fit). The user's constraint was the DSL authoring surface (SizeThatFits.make, Fit.of, etc.) + behavior visible to developers. Adding a method to Emitter (already public, internal transport) is acceptable and invisible to DSL authors.

But can I avoid it? The flag could be set via the `mount` signature... also public. Or an Environment value. Or: server-core constructs the emitter — actually simplest: since the plan's option 1 explicitly mentioned a package-private flag + setter, and server-core is a separate module, package-private won't work across Maven modules. So it must be a public-but-internal method on Emitter. That's fine — Emitter is already public and is plumbing, not the authoring DSL.

Let me design:
- `Emitter`: add `private boolean fullSnapshot;` and a method `public Emitter withFullSnapshotChildren(boolean)` returning this (fluent) OR just `public void enableSnapshotChildren()`. Keep it documented as internal transport. Actually the cleanest for server-core: `new Emitter(sink, theme).snapshotChildren()` returning this.

Wait, actually — let me reconsider whether renderFull needs it too. renderFull() re-emits the retained tree. If mount built the tree with all candidates (because snapshotChildren was on), renderFull re-emits all candidates automatically — no need to toggle during renderFull. So the flag only matters during mount's render. 

So:
- Emitter field `boolean emitAllFitCandidates` (package — but needs to be set from server-core → public setter).
- In `FitSlot.render`, how does it read the emitter's flag? FitSlot.render doesn't have a reference to the emitter. Options:
  1. A ThreadLocal on Emitter that FitSlot reads (would need a public static — ugly).
  2. Express the mode through the `Environment` — e.g. a boolean on the mount Environment, or a dedicated EnvironmentKey. This is actually elegant: `Environment.within`/scoped value. But FitSlot reads `Environment.current()` already. Add an internal EnvironmentKey<Boolean> for snapshot mode? That's a public static constant on Environment — public API additive change (invisible to authors, but public).
  3. Pass the flag via PathlandNode: FitSlot can read Environment, but the render is driven by the outer `mount(root, env)` call. We could set the flag on the `Environment` object? The `Environment` passed to mount is the session env; FitSlot receives `Environment env` in render(env).

  Hmm, actually FitSlot.render(env) — env is Environment. But the snapshot flag is about emission, not authoring. ThreadLocal on Environment is the mechanism ("this thread-local is the implementation of the environment"). We could add `Environment.withSnapshotEmission(true)` — but that changes Environment's public API.

Let me reconsider: simplest minimal exposure. The cleanest option that's invisible to DSL authors yet works across modules: a **package-private ThreadLocal in `com.pathland.view`** consulted by FitSlot... but server-core is in `com.pathland.server`, can't touch package-private.

OK let me think about what's truly minimal and clean:

Option R: **PathlandNode-stored flag decided by server-core**. No—FitSlot builds the node.

Option S: **A public ThreadLocal on a public-but-internal holder in com.pathland.view**, e.g. a static on `SizeThatFits` or a small `FitSlot` internal switch: `public static boolean snapshotChildren = false;` set by server-core before mount, read by FitSlot.render, reset after. `SizeThatFits` is public (it's the DSL surface!)  - adding a static there is visible. Not great.

Option T: **Constructor flag on Emitter + a package-private static ThreadLocal in `com.pathland.view`** that Emitter sets and FitSlot reads. Both classes: Emitter is in `com.pathland.view.emit`, FitSlot in `com.pathland.view`. Package-private static won't cross packages either.

Ugh, the package boundary (com.pathland.view vs com.pathland.view.emit) is the crux. 

Wait — actually, does FitSlot need the flag at all? Let me reconsider. The retained tree is built once. If we want the LIVE (non-SSR) Java fit slots to keep emitting ONE child (byte-identical live behavior + existing tests), but the SSR session's fit slots to emit ALL... the difference has to flow through mount.

Actually, maybe the simplest and most aligned-with-plan approach: make the mode an **`Environment` internal scope** — since Environment is the one thing threaded through both mount and FitSlot.render, and it's explicitly the "environment implementation", scoping a hidden value there is idiomatic. `EnvironmentValues` has `with(key, value)` (I saw EnvironmentValues keyed map). Add an **internal EnvironmentKey<Boolean> FIT_SNAPSHOT** (package-private field? Environment is public; a package-private static field on it is invisible to server-core — but server-core must SET it).

Hmm, server-core would need a public route.

Then a package-private static ThreadLocal `EMITTING_SNAPSHOT` on... no.

Cleanest within the package structure: since `emit` and `view` are sibling packages, the flag must be reachable from both. The simplest mechanism that keeps the DSL surface (View/SizeThatFits/Fit) 100% untouched: **`Environment`**. Add to `EnvironmentValues` support for the flag, and expose a public but internal static on `Environment`? That's still Environment public API.

Alternatively — **don't read the flag in FitSlot at all.** Instead: keep `FitSlot.render` building the node with a SINGLE visible child as today, but ALSO wire all candidates into `node.children`? That changes what's emitted at mount for everyone.

OK here's the cleanest final design — **a public ThreadLocal-based switch consumed via Environment, but exposed through Emitter only**:

Actually, you know what — let me just make the flag flow through **`Environment`'s existing ThreadLocal VALUES mechanism using an internal key with a package-private constant**, AND give server-core a public way to arm it: a public static method on `Environment` is public API. 

Let me reconsider if there's a way that changes NO public surface of pathland-view at all (pure "Option 1 internal"):

Let me design A2 fully and precisely, addressing every corner up front so there's no more circling:

## The A2 design

Flow:
1. SSR mount frame: SIZE_THAT_FITS emits ALL candidates as children (in FIT_QUERY sorted order). Each child wrapped in the renderer by `data-pathland-fit-cand` + a container div with band rules.
2. Client hydrates SSR, sees N candidates + container queries; first paint correct via CSS.
3. WS opens. Client's ResizeObserver measures, reports FIT_CHANGED(index).
4. Server: fitIndex signal updates → structural effect fires → reconcileSlot. For snapshot form (children.size()>1), it downgrades: emits TREE deltas replacing N children with the single selected child.
5. Client applies deltas: removes extra wrappers, keeps the selected wrapper's inner element; removes container-name/band rules → slot is now plain single-child, live model continues with normal ResizeObserver + FIT_CHANGED on transitions.

Key challenges to nail down ONCE:

### A. How does FitSlot know it's in snapshot mode?
Option 1 (thread-local): Emitter sets a package-private static ThreadLocal around `root.render(env)` in mount/renderFull. But `comm.pathland.view.SizeThatFits` is a different package from `com.pathland.view.emit.Emitter`. package-private won't cross. So need public API or a different channel.

Option 2: Put the flag on `PathlandNode` is wrong (FitSlot renders before node exists... actually FitSlot creates the node). Hmm, FitSlot.render creates PathlandNode and adds children. It could read a static flag.

Actually the cleanest: a **static ThreadLocal on `Emitter`**, public but documented internal. Or put it on `PathlandNode`? No, FitSlot already imports PathlandNode (com.pathland.view.emit.PathlandNode). FitSlot can read `PathlandNode.snapshotEmission` thread-local. But that's a public static on PathlandNode. Hmm.

Alternatively: Emitter could expose the flag via a public static ThreadLocal on a small internal class. But the requirement is "invisible to developers" — internal plumbing can be public-ish as long as it's clearly internal and not the authoring API.

Actually simplest: `PathlandNode` gets a `public static final ThreadLocal<Boolean> SNAPSHOT_EMISSION` — FitSlot reads it, Emitter sets it. Both are in the same module `pathland-view`. Static thread-local, no public surface beyond a documented-internal static. Fine.

### B. When is snapshot mode on?
- `mount`: yes (the SSR frame)
- `renderFull` (META::RESYNC): yes (re-sends full tree; should match what SSR sent, keeping all candidates so the client can re-hydrate container queries). Actually resync after downgrade... we should send the current retained tree. If downgraded, it's 1 child. Hmm. Let me think.

The retained tree: at mount, FitSlot.render with snapshot on → node.children = all candidates. Later FIT_CHANGED → reconcileSlot downgrades node.children to 1. So the retained tree *state* changes. renderFull just re-emits the retained tree.

But here's the subtlety: if the renderer rendered all-candidates at mount, and then the client reconnects and calls resync, the retained tree is now single-child (downgraded). renderFull would emit 1 child — and the client, having container-query gated N wrappers, would need to handle N→1 via the emitted deltas. No—wait, at mount node.children was populated by FitSlot.render with all candidates) against fresh (1 child) → emits removes for N-1 candidates! That's the immediate-downgrade-at-mount problem. The first FIT_CHANGED (maybe index 0 again, or index 1) triggers it. We want: before any report, keep N. After first report, downgrade to the reported selection.

`fitReported` set by fitInput before fitIndex.set. reconcileSlot gate: if !fitReported and children>1 → no-op (keep N). But the structural effect's immediate first run at mount also calls reconcileSlot → gate → no-op → good.

But there's another wrinkle: `registerBindings(node)` for a structural slot does NOT recurse into children (line 300-308). So the N candidates' subtrees never get bindings registered at mount in snapshot mode! That means candidate 2's internal Text signals won't re-emit... but wait, candidates are all rendered; only the visible one matters. Actually — think about what happens after downgrade. Once FIT_CHANGED arrives and we downgrade to 1 child, reconcileSlot:
- renders structuralContent (selectedView = the chosen candidate)
- reconciles old children (N) vs new (1)
- destroys old subtree bindings, re-registers new

So after downgrade, only the selected candidate's subtree has bindings. The non-selected candidates' subtrees are gone from the wire. That's fine — they're not shown.

But BEFORE any FIT_CHANGED (during the SSR window), do we need candidate bindings? The SSR DOM is already rendered with all candidates (static content at mount). If a signal changes before the first FIT_CHANGED... the SSR page is what the client sees until JS connects. For no-JS, signals never change anyway. Registering bindings for ALL N candidates at mount would be more correct for "work with deltas while N is shown" — e.g., a text update to the *visible* candidate while still in N-form (before report). But the report comes right after WS open, so the window is milliseconds. I'll note this but keep it simple: N-candidate form is only for SSR first paint + until first report. After first report it's single-child with full bindings. To be safe though, we could register bindings for all candidates at mount in snapshot mode (recurse). That's cheap and makes the SSR-live N-form fully reactive. ### C. The immediate effect problem — really nail it

```

    EffectRef structural = Signals.effect(() -> reconcileSlot(node));  // runs immediately
    ...

And reconcileSlot on downgrade destroys all + re-registers just the single. ✓

### D. reconcileSlot downgrade emission
When FIT_CHANGED arrives:
- fitInput: fitReported=true; fitSelection=index; fitIndex.set(index)
- structural effect re-runs → reconcileSlot
- gate now passes (fitReported true). Render structuralContent → 1 fresh child. Diff old (N) vs new (1). reconcileChildren emits removes + deleteNode for extra, create/insert for kept. slot.children becomes [fresh]. 
- The kept child: fresh is a re-render of the selected candidate. If the old child at position `index` has the same component, id reused? reconcileChildren matches by position+component. old = [cand0, cand1, ...], new = [selected]. Position 0: old=cand0 vs fresh=selected. If selected is cand1 (different component), then i=0: old!=null fresh!=null, component mismatch → remove cand0, create selected at 0. i=1: old=cand1 vs fresh=null → remove cand1. So the selected candidate gets a NEW id and the SSR's copy of cand1 is deleted. 

Wait — this is the id-stability concern again. The SSR emitted cand1 with some id (say 11). The downgrade emits REMOVE cand1(11) + CREATE cand1(new id 20) + INSERT. The client needs to remove the old wrapper(11) and add a new element(20). The client's N→1 cleanup then: after applying deltas, remove any leftover `data-pathland-fit-cand` wrappers and container-name/band rules. Since the deltas already removed/deleted the old candidates (all N removed, fresh one inserted bare without wrapper... hmm, but the client inserts the fresh child into the slot via INSERT_CHILD — the fresh child is bare, no wrapper). 

So the client flow for the downgrade:
- Server emits REMOVE_CHILD(parent, candIds...) + DELETE_NODE for all N old children
- CREATE_NODE + INSERT_CHILD for the single fresh selected child
- Client applies: all wrappers gone, one bare child inserted. Client then notices the slot no longer has `[data-pathland-fit-cand]` wrappers, removes `container-name`/`container-type` style (or just leaves container-name, harmless) and removes band rules from the `<style data-pathland-fit>` block.
